title: The mean distance to a simple closed curve on the sphere
summary: Kimberling's Problem 10 asks for a simple closed curve of prescribed length $L$ (in particular, $L=4π$) on the unit sphere minimizing the mean geodesic distance $\mathcal{J}$ from a point of the sphere to the curve. For a positive integer $n$, put $\vartheta_{n}=π/(2n)$ and $L_{n}=2π/\sin\vartheta_{n}$. We show that the minimum of $\mathcal{J}$ over rectifiable simple closed curves of length at most $L_{n}$ equals $\vartheta_{n}-\tan(\vartheta_{n}/2)$, that it is attained only by curves of length exactly $L_{n}$, and that the sphere-filling ropes $β^{n,k}$ of Gerlach and von der Mosel attain…
